identification: Victorian-style carving/butcher's sharpening steel, round tapered steel rod about 30-35cm overall (est. from photo), turned light hardwood handle (boxwood/beech-type, not horn or bone) with dark spiral-scored grip bands on the lower half, brass collar and flared brass guard at the steel end, brass knop finial with a brass/copper hanging ring. Likely late 19th to early 20th century, English or colonial. A round hole about 5-6mm in the handle near the finial end (looks like a knot/drilled or bored hole, not general worm). Steel has dark patina, no obvious pitting in photo. Estimate 20-50, current bid $20.
